parameters: Sitting on the upper deck, I sink my teeth into moss-covered
bread. The de-icing is still rough going.
The captain's disease shows no prospects of subsiding.
He cannot get up from the bed and only mutters some
The morale of the crew continues to sink.
People desert the ship, succumb to illness, or freeze
to death. There’s barely anyone I recognize left.
We have mountains of food, and yet nothing we can eat.
Some even began to eat the flesh of their dead comrades to
stay alive. One of them offered it to me lying that it's
turtle soup...I declined. I've already given up on life.
No point living till I'm some senile old codger.
"What's gonna taste worse, your corpse, or your homeland's
cooking?", a young sailor lets out a dry laugh.
I try to join in his merry, but my lips are frozen shut.
